checks: The minimum of the three affine functions is concave and each vertex value is at least eight, so every real base radius is at least R+1. The defining inequalities are affine when the three bounds are imposed separately. Q has interior, the radii are positive, and compactness follows from bounded Q and bounded radii. The simplex scale gives the stated fiber volumes and true centroids for d=1 as well.

Using the full eight-base census, the complement radii are s,s+3/8 and F has radii s+3/4,s+1,s+1/2,s,s+1/4,s. Subtracting three copies of the complement sum leaves precisely the four displayed differences of positive powers. Each comparison is strict for s≥1 and d≥1, so W_F−3(T−W_F)>0 and W_F/3>T/4.

Independent integer arithmetic at R=1,d=2 gives (256,361,484,576,400,256,324,256) in units |Delta_2|/64. E contributes 1101, F contributes 2296, their shared index 2 contributes 484, and 1101+2296−484=2913 equals the eight-weight sum.

The map (z,t) ↦ (z,(R+t/8)·1/(d+1)) is affine and injective for d≥1, with an affine inverse on its image. This preserves the relative Helly number by restricting convex sets to the affine span. The two accepted depth facts apply to closed ambient caps, first for the F atoms and then for the full positive fibers. Adding the other atoms cannot decrease cap weight. Dividing the raw bound by the positive total mass gives the claimed normalized inequality.

Verified both source hashes and locators. Section 2 of f1f97e5764053b3f gives the same strict four-term comparison, special weights and planar-face payment. Sections 1 and 4 of 588eabf65d9a1440 give the actual simplex model, all positive fibers and the special weight units. The latter source’s additional d=2 specific two-pair bound is separate.

For these simplex fibers the ordinary maximum is at the centroid by symmetry and concavity and scales with the radius, and the second affine roof plane touches exactly F, which has three occupied parities. The accepted theorem supplies no original eight-base census or strict mass comparison.

summary: For every R≥0 and integer d≥1, the original simplex profile has W_F>3T/4. Its six-point centroid patch therefore contains an actual mark of normalized mixed depth at least gamma_d W_F/(3T), strictly above gamma_d/4.
